registration: docs/efv-2026-08-07b/FEATURE_LEAK_GATE.md sections 0-4, written in full before this lab existed and before any accuracy number was computed
lane: D wave 2: feature-level label leak + as-of anchor selection (plan item E1)
estimator: forward-chained over efv_model.SCORED_YEARS (11 folds), pair-weighted Spearman, primitives imported from tools/efv_mde_lab.py; paired bootstrap resamples the WHOLE pool and refits BOTH arms on the same draw; MDE95 = 1.96 * sd(contrast), two-sided
self_added_threshold: PRIMARY BAR IS THE PAIRED-CONTRAST MDE95, not the model-vs-consensus MDE95_POOLED_RHO (0.044 hit / 0.0436 pit) that earlier drop gates used. Two fits of the same model differing in one column share nearly all their sampling variability, so the model-vs-consensus floor is far too WIDE here, and a too-wide floor is the PERMISSIVE direction for the NULL verdicts this lane produces (standing rule F). Both are reported on every contrast: see resolvable_paired vs resolvable_legacy_floor.

identity_stale_is_cutlag_minus_label.claim: stale == cut_lag - 1[kind == debuted]. `stale` is not a measurement of feature freshness, it is cut_lag with the LABEL subtracted into it by the decision_year convention.

identity_window_is_cutoff_year_minus_1.claim: first_season == cutoff_year - 1 for both kinds. After the 2026-07-24 as-of repair the MiLB feature WINDOW is a function of the cutoff DATE alone and the rule is identical for busts and debuted rows.

hit.criterion: |win_lag kind-mean gap| >= 0.25 seasons, OR any win_lag cell with n >= 50 and P(bust) outside [0.05, 0.95]
